title: Introduce sparse probe aggregator and compact release epitome generator
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding churn and large auto-generated changelogs make human review slow and increase noise in release briefs. The sparse-probe-aggregator consolidates sampled probe outputs from onboarding telemetry into compact, de-duplicated 'epitomes' and emits a compatibility fingerprint used by downstream changelog synthesizers. This PR adds a background aggregator, a canonical epitope serialization format, and a small changelog 'epitome-to-blurb' converter that the release composer can call to produce terse, reviewable release snippets.

What this includes (high level): - New aggregator service (go) that consumes probe events from telemetry Kafka topic and produces epitope records to the model-registry DB (epitopes table). - Epitope protobuf schema and JSON serializer that captures fingerprint, representative prompts/responses, coverage stats and a small entropy sketch. - A compat-fingerprint generator that summarizes variant-affinity vectors; used by the release pipeline to mark likely-breaking variant changes. - Changelog-epitome adapter (python) that converts epitope records to the compact 'release epitome' used in release notes and the curator UI. - Backfill job to generate epitopes for the last 90 days of telemetry (configurable). - Feature-flag gating (ff:epitome_autogen) so we can rollout gradually.

Design notes: - Aggregation is sparse: probes are sampled with a configurable reservoir and deduplicated using a locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) pass plus a lightweight LRU-k dedupe buffer to avoid storing near-duplicates. - Epitopes are intentionally small (target ~1-2KB JSON payload) and include a coverage histogram (sequence length buckets), top-3 tokens entropy, and a coherence score used by the epitome-to-blurb converter to prioritize candidate lines. - The compat-fingerprint is a 64-bit hashed vector (protobuf repeated uint32) derived from model variant affordance tags + top-10 probe signatures; it's cheap to compare and stable across minor probe noise.

Migration and rollout: - DB migration: add epitopes table and index on model_version_id + fingerprint (migration included). - Backfill is optional and gated behind ff:epitome_backfill; initial run created ~72k epitopes from 90d of telemetry (dry-run mode available). - Default: autogen disabled. On rollout we will enable for a small cohort of internal models, monitor release-epitome size and curator feedback before widening.

Checklist: - [x] Add aggregator service and core LSH/dedupe pipeline - [x] Protobuf/JSON schema + serializer - [x] Changelog adapter and UI contract sample - [x] DB migration and index - [x] Backfill job + dry-run mode - [x] Unit tests (go + python) and e2e integration harness - [x] Feature flags and docs - [x] Performance benchmark and storage estimate

Testing & Benchmarks: - Unit test coverage added: aggregator (go) 86%, adapter (py) 91%. - Integration: local harness with 10k synthetic probe events shows stable throughput ~2.8k events/s on a single aggregate worker and memory < 1.2GB. - Release-note compression: a sampling across 120 model changes showed median changelog size reduced by 35% and reviewer-edit time reduced by ~22% in a small internal trial.

Operational notes: - New metrics: epitome_ingest.rate, epitome_ingest.latency_p50/p95, epitome_dedupe.rate, epitome_backfill.progress. - Alerts: high p95 ingestion latency or error spikes will automatically flip ff:epitome_autogen to off via the rollout playbook. - Costs: expected DB storage increase ~1.2GB/month for current internal traffic; we included TTL policy (epitopes retain 180 days by default).

Why this is different from existing changelog automation: instead of verbatim probe dumps we synthesize a deterministic, compact representation that preserves representative examples and quantifies coverage/uncertainty; that enables much smaller release snippets and faster human triage while keeping the provenance link to original probe ids for deep inspection.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the LSH dedupe heuristics and the compat fingerprint stability tests. The protos include forward-compatible fields; if reviewers want a stricter schema we can add validation hooks before the backfill runs.

review_conversation: Miguel Rivera: Nice design, Asha. Two asks: (1) can you add a stability test that injects minor probe noise and verifies fingerprint stays stable for <=2% change, (2) please document the TTL policy in the migration note.
Asha Patel: Added a stability test and expanded migration docs to include TTL and backfill cost estimate (see migrations/20260201_add_epitopes_table.sql comments).
Jian Li: Found a race in the aggregator worker pool shutdown path — suggested fix applied in commit 5. Resolved locally, please confirm no extra goroutines leak on failed Kafka reconnects.
Asha Patel: applied pool shutdown fix and added test that simulates reconnect transient failure. CI shows transient fail on first run but passes after retry (CI re-run recorded below).
Priya Narayanan: Small nit on the epitome JSON key naming (use 'coverage_hist' instead of 'coverageBuckets'). Fixed in adapter commit. Approving once CI green.
CI Bot: build/linux: failed on first run (flaky test TestAggregator_Retry), rerun triggered by @asha, build/linux: pass, lint: pass, pytests: pass, integration: pass
release_notes: Adds a sparse probe aggregation pipeline and compact 'epitome' serialization used to synthesize shorter, reviewable release snippets; includes DB migration, backfill tooling, feature flags, and a rollout playbook. Initial rollout gated behind ff:epitome_autogen. Expected changelog size reduction and improved reviewer efficiency.
notes_for_ops: Monitor epitome_ingest.latency_p95 and epitome_backfill.progress. If p95 > 2s for 5m, flip ff:epitome_autogen to off and page on-call. Backfill should be run during low-traffic windows; runs include dry-run mode. Storage TTL default 180 days; change via deployment config.
owner_patch_summary: Rolled out in canary to 3 internal models for 2 weeks, iterated LSH params (k=6, bands=4) to optimize dedupe without over-collapsing. Backfill created 72k epitopes for 90d and was kept in dry-run until ops validated size and quality.
